description: Single-file compile/verify benchmark corpus for upstream rustc, tRust noverify, explicit tRust LLVM, tRust verification, and experimental trust-cg slots.

upstream-rustc.notes: Rust baseline compile/codegen slot. Flawed programs are expected to compile because the bugs are semantic proof obligations.

trust-noverify.notes: Trust compiler with -Z trust-verify=off. This is the verifier-disabled compile/codegen comparison slot.

llvm.notes: Trust compiler with -Z trust-verify=off and -Z codegen-backend=llvm. This forces the production LLVM backend for explicit LLVM-vs-trust-cg parity comparisons.

trust-verify.notes: Trust compiler with native verification JSON transport. Good programs should prove; flawed programs should emit failed obligations.

trust-cg.notes: Trust compiler with -Z trust-verify=off and -Z codegen-backend=trust_cg. trust-cg is experimental and report-only by default.

classes.meaning: The selected Trust sysroot has no rustc_codegen_trust_cg backend or the selected compiler rejects the trust-cg backend flag.
trust-cg was selected, but lowering, verification, optimization, register allocation, or object emission failed before producing an object.
trust-cg reached native linkage/runtime machinery that the compile-only benchmark does not execute by default.
trust-cg failed for a reason that was not recognized by the runner classifier.

coverage_model.known_program_policy: Every benchmark program is explicitly paired as a known-good or known-flawed variant. Compile slots should accept both variants; the trust-verify slot should prove known-good variants and reject known-flawed variants.

tiers.description: Algorithmic examples that exercise realistic control flow and indexing before verification-specific safety kernels.
Focused safety obligations used to measure verifier and backend behavior with direct good/flawed counterparts.
Formatter-free low-cost candidate pairs that extend proof-design coverage into ADTs, iterators, borrowing, and recursion before they become release gates.
Known-good/known-flawed adversarial pairs organized by verifier behavior target. These rows are deliberately not greenwashed: every current trust-verify deviation is tied to a named expected gap.

target_groups.description: Path-sensitive branch predicates and short-circuit guard preservation.
Loop-carried slice bounds and termination/invariant proof strength.
Callee summaries that must preserve preconditions across helper calls.
Enum/struct state agreement and ADT invariant modeling.
Slice fat-pointer metadata, raw pointer bounds, and provenance-sensitive reads.
Formatter and allocation-heavy std surfaces kept separate from formatter-free fixtures.
Flawed rows that should produce a counterexample or repair candidate for strengthening a missing guard.

expectation_model.purpose: Declarative expected outcomes for compile, verify, runtime parity, backward-pass/backprop, LLVM, trust-cg, and documented exception accounting. This is fixture metadata, not runner code.
expectation_model.exception_hook_policy: Every non-trust-cg exception to these expectations must be named in expected_known_gaps and referenced here. trust-cg exceptions are represented by trust_cg_exception_model classes.

expected_known_gaps.reason: Adversarial path guard rows document the current need for proof-grade path predicate preservation before the good variant can be a release gate or the flawed variant can require repair evidence.

stderr_contains_any: MIR router has no proof-grade zani encoding
expected_known_gaps.reason: Adversarial loop rows require loop-carried slice-bound invariants and termination evidence; current zani/MIR transport can leave these obligations unknown or runtime-checked.
Adversarial interprocedural rows require helper summaries to preserve denominator preconditions across calls before they can become hard gates.
Adversarial data-model rows intentionally require enum tag and struct-state reasoning that is not yet consistently proof-grade in the native verifier.
Adversarial memory rows exercise slice fat-pointer metadata and raw-pointer provenance, which remain documented verifier modeling gaps rather than hidden green rows.
Adversarial std/format rows deliberately cross allocation and formatter MIR so formatter-heavy proof gaps remain accounted separately from formatter-free fixtures.
Adversarial backprop rows keep a missing-guard repair target visible until verifier transport reliably carries counterexample or repair-candidate payloads with source attribution.
